text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to $150.80, capping a remarkable two-week rally of 12.45%. The move tracks directly with oil prices surging to six-month highs—Brent crude crossed $116 per barrel today—driven by escalating Middle East tensions and U.S. threats of military action against Iran. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits immediately when crude prices spike, since higher oil translates to higher revenue and profits per barrel produced.

The broader story here is that geopolitical risk in the Middle East has become the dominant market driver. News of U.S. diplomats withdrawing from Saudi Arabia, reported plans for renewed strikes on Iran, and Houthi attacks on oil infrastructure have convinced investors that regional conflict could tighten global oil supply. That risk premium is flowing directly into energy stocks, and companies like ConocoPhillips—which pump oil regardless of where prices come from—are seeing their valuations reset upward as traders bet on sustained higher prices.
